topic.title: Transferability, Source Selection, and Generalization Guarantees
topic.overview: Transfer learning uses knowledge from source tasks to improve learning on a target task with limited data. This cluster asks when transfer helps, how task similarity should be measured, and how much information to use from each source. Theoretical analyses relate achievable target error to source and target sample sizes, model capacity, and task relatedness.
topic.whyItMatters: More source data is not automatically beneficial. Measuring transferability can help avoid negative transfer and allocate training effort toward sources whose information is relevant to the target rather than merely abundant.
topic.evolution: Early representatives use transferred discriminability, priors, and boosting. Later work develops minimax limits and multi-source weighting. Recent papers optimize source sample quantities, analyze feature dependence, and construct finite sets of candidate parameter-efficient adaptations to obtain informative few-shot generalization certificates.
openQuestions: How can relatedness be estimated reliably from very little target data?
Which guarantees remain useful when source tasks were selected adaptively or differ in unmeasured ways?
